clue.text: Is "Bottoms up!" a more face-saving way to toast ?

definitions.text: Is "Bottoms up!" a more face-saving way to toast ?

parts.words: Is "Bottoms up!" a more face-saving way to toast ?
parts.note: a drinking toast built round the face: the clue asks whether a toast naming the nose beats one naming the bottom

explanation.surface: Someone at a party wonders whether one drinking toast is more polite than another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here's skin off your nose' is an old drinking toast; 'face-saving' points at the nose, the face's feature, against 'Bottoms up!'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a traditional drinking salutation, the same kind of thing as 'Bottoms up!' or 'Cheers'.

clue.text: Camp-follower from Ulster

indicators.note: made from the letters of Ulster, which are rearranged to give a new word

explanation.surface: A hanger-on of an army turns out to come from Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals that the letters of ULSTER are rearranged. Ulster is the northern province of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A sutler was a trader who followed an army and sold provisions to the soldiers, a classic camp-follower.

clue.text: That Roman convict had up for such a deed?

parts.note: ille is the Latin word for 'that', so a Roman would say it

indicators.note: in a down clue, being had up raises the word, so it is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lag is slang for a convict, as in 'old lag'

explanation.surface: A Roman criminal is brought to court for some offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had up' turns LAG to GAL beneath ILLE. 'had up' also suggests being charged in court, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An unlawful act is a deed of the sort a convict might be charged with.

clue.text: Timely knocking, back of too much Italian, and one French

indicators.note: knocking back a drink downs it; here it means the word is turned round

parts.note: troppo is Italian for 'too much', as in the musical direction 'non troppo'
une is the French feminine word for 'one'

explanation.surface: Someone drinks too much Italian wine at just the right moment, with a French companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back of' reverses TROPPO into OPPORT. The surface makes 'knocking back' sound like drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well timed arrives at a convenient, favourable moment.

clue.text: Flourished tho cat with an impatient movement

parts.note: fl. is the abbreviation for floruit, Latin for 'flourished', used of the dates a person was active
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: A cat waved its tail about and stalked off in a huff.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'the cat'. FL is the reference-book abbreviation for 'flourished'.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounce is to fling oneself about or storm off in irritation, an impatient movement.

clue.text: Mainly descriptive ?

parts.note: the main is an old word for the sea, so a word describing the main is one about the sea

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things of the open sea, which poets call the main.

clue.text: Stir up the river

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river on maps
the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire and another in East Anglia, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Someone is told to churn up the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the river' gives both R (river) and OUSE, the river: one phrase, two pieces. The Ouse is a river in England.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse a crowd or feelings is to stir them up or awaken them.

clue.text: Cue for exit in a sketch ?

definitions.meaning: an actor's line telling them to go off stage could be called an ...
a rough drawing showing only the shape of something

explanation.surface: In a comedy sketch, one line tells the performer to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue to go out is a line of script; separately, a rough draft or drawing gives only the main lines of something.

clue.text: Old Italian courtesan loses nothing, oddly enough

indicators.note: the letters of courtesan are rearranged in an odd way once one is taken from them

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An Italian courtesan of old somehow gets by without any money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes the O (nothing) away from COURTESAN; 'oddly enough' then rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscans lived in central Italy before the Romans, so one of them is an ancient Italian.

clue.text: Its ring is no sign of engagement

definitions.text: Its ring is no sign of engagement

parts.words: Its ring is no sign of engagement
parts.note: a ring that means the line is free, not engaged, as opposed to an engagement ring

explanation.definitionFit: When the line is busy you hear the engaged tone; hearing it ring means the device at the other end is not in use.

clue.text: Speak out and out

definitions.meaning: to say aloud or voice words

explanation.surface: Someone is told to speak up and keep at it.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to voice something; as an adjective it means total or complete, as in a total fool.

clue.text: A Poet (curtailed)

parts.note: cutting the tail off the word poet leaves Poe, so the clue reads as Mr A. Poe, and his first name is wanted

explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe signed himself Edgar A. Poe, so the A in that name stands next to his first name.

clue.text: Sunnier but changeable round the North-east for the sisters

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation, holding it inside
changeable weather is unsettled, so the letters of sunnier are unsettled into a new order

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: Nuns move to the north-east, where the weather is sunnier but more fickle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changeable' looks like a comment on the weather but signals the anagram; 'round' signals the container. The definition is a loose 'places for the sisters'.
explanation.definitionFit: Convents house communities of nuns, who are called sisters.

clue.text: Santa has a point in the contract

parts.note: Santa Claus, Father Christmas
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Father Christmas has a point to make about a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: E for east is one of the four compass points, a common crossword piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause is one separate provision or article written into a contract.

clue.text: Monster bells by an artist

parts.note: a chime is a set of tuned bells
RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: An artist depicts a monster alongside some ringing bells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places one piece beside the other. RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the chimera was a fire-breathing beast with a lion's head, a goat's body and a serpent's tail.

clue.text: I'm quick in service, mostly, but entirely unrehearsed

annotationWithheld.why: I'm quick in service, mostly, but entirely unrehearsed (9): I'M + PROMPT (quick) accounts for IMPROMPT, but no reading of 'in service, mostly' gives the final U, and no source gives the parse
annotationWithheld.clue: I'm quick in service, mostly, but entirely unrehearsed

clue.text: Her fruit upsets everybody

parts.note: a prune is a dried plum

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting a word tips it over so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: all means everybody, as in 'all agreed'

explanation.surface: A woman's fruit sends everyone flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsets' turns ALL to LLA after PRUNE. 'Her' stands for a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's given name, so it stands for a particular woman, a she.

clue.text: Noisy game ? Shady practices rather

definitions.meaning: a game named after a din: a racket is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A loud game turns out to involve some rather dodgy goings-on.
explanation.walkthrough: Rackets is a fast court game, a forerunner of squash; the question mark flags that 'noisy' plays on a racket meaning a din.
explanation.definitionFit: The ball game and the plural of din share a spelling; criminal scams are also called by the same word.

clue.text: Drawing a vehicle with nothing on

parts.note: a cart is a simple wheeled vehicle
O looks like zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A picture shows a car with nobody in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous drawing in a newspaper, or the full-size sketch for a painting, is called this.

clue.text: Pin up for knocking down

parts.note: a pin stood upright so that it can be bowled over, not a pin-up picture

explanation.definitionFit: In ninepins or skittles each wooden pin is set up only to be knocked over by a thrown ball.

clue.text: Up in the pass, a dome

indicators.note: the first word is placed inside the word for the pass

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: High in a mountain pass someone sees a dome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks like a direction but supplies its own two letters; 'in' is the container signal. A col is a mountain pass, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupola is a small rounded dome on top of a roof.

clue.text: Play score in quintuplicate

parts.note: a score is twenty, so five scores make a hundred, a total a batsman can reach in play

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a hundred runs scored by one batsman in an innings, five times twenty, has this name.

clue.text: Civet cat of Borneo gives clue for " Slang"

parts.note: the word slang is the letter L placed inside the word sang

explanation.surface: A Bornean civet's name happens to be a clue to a common word.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, split up, reads as a clue whose solution is SLANG.
explanation.definitionFit: The linsang is a slender, civet-like carnivore of the forests of South-East Asia, including Borneo.

clue.text: Not that his works make an uninteresting study

definitions.text: Not that his works make an uninteresting study

parts.words: Not that his works make an uninteresting study
parts.note: a dull study, read as a dull den, names a poet, while the clue denies his writing is dull

explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was the English poet laureate of the Restoration, author of 'Absalom and Achitophel'.

clue.text: His solo turn is' capital

parts.note: the word solo with its letters turned about gives a capital city, so the clue's man is from that country

explanation.definitionFit: Rearrange SOLO and you get Oslo, the capital of Norway, so the man is from there.

clue.text: Robert E is worried about her

indicators.note: worried fodder is shaken about, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: General Lee is anxious about a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges LEE and IS together; 'about' is the link to 'her', a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's given name, so it stands for a particular woman.

clue.text: Man of property

parts.note: a person who holds title to something

explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who possesses something is its proprietor; 'The Man of Property' is also Galsworthy's novel.

clue.text: Tower of London's. pride once

parts.note: pride is the group word for big cats, and the Tower of London once kept a royal menagerie

explanation.definitionFit: A group of these big cats is called a pride, and the medieval royal menagerie at the Tower housed them.

clue.text: Something tricky up your sleeve ?

parts.note: a winning card at bridge, or an ace a cheat hides up a sleeve, used here of a hidden advantage

explanation.definitionFit: A card from the leading suit that wins a trick is a hidden advantage kept in reserve.

clue.text: A musical call to arms

parts.note: a stage show whose title tells a sharpshooting woman to pick up her weapon

explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin's 1946 show about the markswoman Annie Oakley has a title urging her to arm herself.
